boundaries: Original model version2 remains immutable; only the32 named nonallocating members are covered.
All ordinary native goals are Valid; healthy smoke timeout/unknown never proves consistency, source-state satisfiability or an ordinary theorem.

All212 original archived task bytes and every support/definition/declaration are retained and indexed. Source-to-driver formula equivalence and primary-source attribution of every standard theory assertion were not independently reconstructed in this audit; they remain explicit normal WP/compiler/driver/foundation TCB.

Method uses normal installed Frama-C/WP33 and solver binaries through opam. Full historical package/Python/native dependency/loader closure, source-to-binary correctness, actual solver-consumed bytes and continuous before/after runtime immutability are not established by record pins or this passive audit.

The compiler-runtime header aggregate is recorded at use. This audit does not reproduce all1982 header bytes, libclang binding, SDK closure, preprocessing/machdep correspondence or historical parse behavior.
Printed internal-Qed contexts and termination/exit inventory-only CFG results remain normal trusted WP/Qed/CFG results, not standalone independently checked SMT proofs.

Qualified typed input domain is not admitted for an arbitrary incoming C/C++ pointer. Generic source caller, default-model integration, construction/reallocation/move/swap/destruction, element payload computation and full ticket25 acceptance remain open.

assumptions.sentence: The C lowering tool (swdb lower, version 9) lowers the C++ proof unit to C that behaves the same; WP proves the C lowering, not the C++.
clang 22.1.8 parses the C++ proof unit correctly for the C lowering tool.
Frama-C/WP 33.0 generates only sound proof obligations for the C lowering under its memory model and the x86_64 machdep.
Z3 5.1.0 answers valid only for valid proof obligations.
CVC5 1.2.1 answers valid only for valid proof obligations.
Alt-Ergo 2.6.4 answers valid only for valid proof obligations.

The exact nonallocating vector C member body is checked under its explicit typed contiguous storage domain. Actual source callers must discharge that domain separately. A defensive at abort is projected only behind its named negated-guard obligation; original contracts, native and CBMC bodies remain unchanged.

source_and_type_qualification.domain_role: qualified original C member body; source caller discharge required
source_and_type_qualification.payload_operations: none: preserves int, float, double and int-pointer element storage exactly

typed_input_domain.caller_discharge: required from actual source vector storage; never inferred from a generic pointer
typed_input_domain.initialization: unchanged original readable/valid predicate; no finite or integer payload surrogate
typed_input_domain.lifetime: receiver and original typed element array remain live throughout the nonallocating call
typed_input_domain.null_case: capacity zero has null data; guarded end performs no null pointer arithmetic

native_properties.description:
assert
  swdb_model_pointer_formation_1:
    ¬(this->size ≡ 0) ⇒
    this->data ≢ \null ∧ \base_addr(this->data) ≡ \base_addr(this->data) ∧
    (\valid_read(this->data) ∨
     (\base_addr(this->data - 1) ≡ \base_addr(this->data) ∧
      \valid_read(this->data - 1))) ∧
    this->data + this->size ≢ \null ∧
    \base_addr(this->data + this->size) ≡ \base_addr(this->data) ∧
    (\valid_read(this->data + this->size) ∨
     (\base_addr((this->data + this->size) - 1) ≡ \base_addr(this->data) ∧
      \valid_read((this->data + this->size) - 1)));

native_properties.description:
assert
  swdb_model_pointer_formation_1:
    ¬(this->size ≡ 0) ⇒
    this->data ≢ \null ∧ \base_addr(this->data) ≡ \base_addr(this->data) ∧
    (\valid_read(this->data) ∨
     (\base_addr(this->data - 1) ≡ \base_addr(this->data) ∧
      \valid_read(this->data - 1))) ∧
    this->data + this->size ≢ \null ∧
    \base_addr(this->data + this->size) ≡ \base_addr(this->data) ∧
    (\valid_read(this->data + this->size) ∨
     (\base_addr((this->data + this->size) - 1) ≡ \base_addr(this->data) ∧
      \valid_read((this->data + this->size) - 1)));
